speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry periodically monitors the sufficiency of supply of over-the-counter medicines in Singapore; (b) if so, what is the periodic interval; (c) what is the amount of emergency stockpile of such medicines to respond quickly to acute nationwide shortages; and (d) whether the Ministry will consider introducing controls against the purchase of such medicines in large quantities for the purpose of sending them out of Singapore.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Health whether an update can be given on the current state of our national stockpile of essential supplies of common over-the-counter medications.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: My response will also cover the matters raised by Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim scheduled for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If necessary, MOH will work with the retailers to procure additional stocks to meet the demand, or issue relevant advisories.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Over the past year, our medical supplies, including oximeters and oxygenators, have been adequate to meet demand.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Retailers therefore persuaded customers to switch to alternate brands which were not in short supply.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First question is in regards to – the Senior Minister of State mentioned that the situation has improved, but given the endemic COVID-19 situation that we are in now, would he see possibilities of over-the-counter medicine running out of stock more frequently?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And in relation to my Parliamentary Question, how often or periodically does MOH or its relevant agencies assess the periodic intervals to assess the stock?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second question is, leaving it to market entities like the Senior Minister of State mentioned, to assess their stock, would it sometimes, at times, depending on the periodic intervals that we check, lead to market failures and lead to runs potentially if there is a global shortage which lead to anxiety in the population.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we assess that in terms of, by either domestic production or diversification of our over-the-counter medicines that will be much in need, given the endemic COVID-19 and going forward as well?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we are fairly confident that we would be able to meet the demands in general.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would put it to the Member that as COVID-19 becomes endemic and, as a population, we treat it and behave towards it like we do other illnesses, there is less chance of the panic buying or the anxiety-induced purchasing that we saw towards the end of last year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, we would be less likely to have similar problems with over-the-counter medication.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If I may also offer some medical advice.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: One way to deal with the anxiety, the routine use of mucolytics and expectorants is not necessary for most of us who have healthy lungs and baseline good health when dealing with an illness such as COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: A variety of generic preparations will do the job just as well.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First, I would like to thank the Senior Minister of State for the impromptu medical advice.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first being, can the Senior Minister of State confirm whether there was a need to tap into the stockpile, given the situation last year.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I think that it is just something that the public is probably interested in knowing.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Did this also affect antigen rapid test (ART) kits and other essential medical supplies, not just over-the-counter (OTC) medications.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And finally, related to the point that the hon Member Saktiandi Supaat raised earlier, in terms of tracking the levels of stockpile of these relevant medications and supplies, does the Ministry use AI, or any other dynamic tracking tools to make sure that while actually maintaining the adequate levels of supply, that we also minimise usage, given that some of these have very finite shelf life?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And indeed, a variety of data and ICT tools are used to manage the supply, as well as the stockpiles at the vendor, as well as the national level.
